this world mission sunday marks the 100th anniversary of its establishment by pope pius xi in 1926. this centenary is an opportunity to celebrate with renewed m issionary zeal. last year, pope leo xiv made an appeal to us in a personal video for world mission sunday. his request echoed around t he world: “please help me help missionaries everywhere.” that’s what world mission sunday does: it helps pope leo care for the 1,130 missionary dioceses and territories under his supervision through the dicastery for evangelization. we are all called to be a part of this missionary work, and we have a singular means to do so: world mission sunday. the second collection we take up today helps extend the church’s evangelisation work to missionary lands where the gospel is being proclaimed for the first time, as well as to places where the church barely exists, or is too young, too persecuted, or to sustain herself. thank you for responding to pope leo’s call to help him help missio naries everywhere! “what does god want from the church in ireland at this time?” the working document for the irish national synodal assembly, which took p lace in gormanston, co. meath, on saturday 17th october 2026, has been published. entitled “is not this what god asks of you?” the document brings together the fru its of five years of prayer, listening and discernment along the irish synodal pathway. it formed the basis for the prayer, conversation, discernment and deliberation of delegates as they p articipated in the national synodal assembly on saturday. but this is not a document for assembly delegates only. the working document belongs within the wider journey of the irish synodal pathway and reflects the voices, hopes, concerns and discernment of people and communities from across the church in ireland. we therefore invite everyone to read it, pray with it and reflect on the question th at has accompanied the synodal pathway from the beginning. visit
